title: Impact of postoperative rehabilitation on outcomes after proximal humerus fracture
summary:
Proximal humerus fractures are among the most common fractures in older adults and represent a significant cause of immobility and functional limitations of the upper extremity, particularly in geriatric patients. Surgical treatment, depending on biological age and fracture morphology, is predominantly performed using plate osteosynthesis or reverse shoulder arthroplasty. Despite clear surgical treatment algorithms, the evidence regarding optimal rehabilitation is limited. In particular, there are few prospective studies that systematically investigate the benefits of standard postoperative treatment regimens involving orthosis and physical therapy. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) is an established method for preventing muscle atrophy and, according to current findings, shows potential for improving joint mobility.

The aim of this prospective randomized study is therefore to evaluate post-treatment regimens with physiotherapy and orthosis versus functional rehabilitation without orthosis and physiotherapy, as well as the application of neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES), on the functional outcome after proximal humerus fracture.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Proximal humerus fracture
Signed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
Minority
Lack of capacity to consent
Pathological fractures
Previous surgeries or pre-existing pathologies of the affected shoulder
Nerve damage to the affected extremity
Polytrauma
Significantly impaired cognitive function
Pre-existing immobility
Pregnancy
Presence of a pacemaker or ICD
Recent thrombosis in the treatment area
